Emitted separately from ev_slope_cole20_2 (same quote) because they are two distinct spatial variables in one targeting rule. FAMILY NOTE: the claim is generic-riparian (it applies to retained/regenerated and to planted buffers alike); no riparian cross_family id exists, so it is filed under the family the source was discovered and screened under (riparian_buffer__natural_restored), per the 2026-09 sweep brief.

relationship.direction: continuity of the riparian buffer along the watercourse network takes precedence over width — narrow CONTINUOUS buffers outperform wide INTERMITTENT ones, so gaps in the existing buffer are the priority restoration targets

quote: To tackle diffuse pollution, narrow continuous buffers are thought to be more effective than wide intermittent buffers (Correll, 2005; Kay et al., 2007). Continuous buffers are also more ef-fective at stabilising water temperatures and increasing ecological connectivity (Correll, 2005; Fischer and Fischenich, 2000).
raw_name: buffer continuity vs intermittency along the watercourse network
attribution: Correll (2005); Kay et al. (2007); Fischer and Fischenich (2000)
selection_justification: Second independent source for the same VONT-gap variable raised from spatial_mcda_riparian_priorities_2013 (buffer gap ratio): buffer CONTINUITY along the network is a first-order siting criterion, which matters directly for a zonal_linear product whose extent is reported as stream length, not pixel area. Encoded as a direction with no numbers because none are stated; the comparison is a design-choice ranking, and the water-quality performance behind it is deferred nbs_effect. FAMILY NOTE: the claim is generic-riparian (it applies to retained/regenerated and to planted buffers alike); no riparian cross_family id exists, so it is filed under the family the source was discovered and screened under (riparian_buffer__natural_restored), per the 2026-09 sweep brief.

context.buffer_type: zoned buffers (a tree zone plus a grass/herbaceous zone)

quote: In productive agricultural catchments, or in smaller farms, zoned buffers may not be economically viable due to the amount of land taken out of production.
raw_name: farm size and adjacent-land productivity as economic-viability constraints on wide zoned buffers
selection_justification: Soft, investment-addressable factor (opportunity cost of land taken out of production) -> operational_risk (M2b Stream-B) and Module-6, never T4 structural suitability. Important for LMIC smallholder pilots: the widest, most multifunctional buffer design is precisely the one that is least viable on small farms, which should surface as a feasibility flag rather than as a suitability mask.

context.context: agricultural riparian buffer strips on productive land

quote: Widening buffers beyond what is necessary, particularly when the adjacent land is highly productive, is not economically viable and can result in re-sistance to adoption (Buckley et al., 2012; Dosskey et al., 2010).
raw_name: landowner resistance to adoption of over-wide buffers (opportunity cost of productive adjacent land)
attribution: Buckley et al. (2012); Dosskey et al. (2010)
selection_justification: Adoption / dis-adoption evidence, routed to operational_risk. Directly qualifies the width rules extracted from this same source: prescribing the widest defensible buffer is self-defeating where adjacent land is productive, which argues for variable-width buffers as a scenario lever rather than a single global width in the T4 surface.

relationship.direction: below 10 persons/km2 the landscape supports WIDE-SCALE restoration (single intervention type, incl. assisted or spontaneous natural regeneration and mixed-species plantations); at 10-100 persons/km2 only MOSAIC restoration applies, spatially mixed with agricultural land uses

quote:
Wide-scale restoration opportunities involve
areas with less intensive land use where a single type of interven-
tion is applied (IUCN and WRI 2014). These areas typically have
a population density below 10/km2, and they account for 21 per-
cent of restoration opportunities worldwide (Laestadius et al.
2012). Approaches suitable for wide-scale restoration include
mixed-species plantations or assisted or spontaneous natural rege-
neration. In areas with higher population density (10–100/km2)
and more intensive land use, mosaic restoration opportunities
encompass larger areas and utilize a combination of interventions
that are spatially mixed with agricultural land uses within the lan-
dscape matrix (Fig. 1).
raw_name: local human population density banding of restoration opportunity (wide-scale vs mosaic)
attribution: IUCN and WRI 2014; Laestadius et al. 2012

For example, in the state of

raw_name: compensation of regeneration stewards for protection costs

relationship.direction: for created and restored wetlands, VERY suitable land lies within about 500 m of a frequently flowing stream; cost and energy rise in buffer steps beyond it (the paper's one-hundred-and-fifty-metre buffers), and land above the highest point where water flows frequently is unsuitable without pumping

quote:
Water availability is a critical factor in selecting wetland location. The distance
from frequently flowing streams has a strong influence on the total cost of the
wetland restoration or creation project. Very suitable areas were considered those
within ∼500 m from a frequently flowing stream. Long distances imply high energy
requirements and financial expenditures. Buffers of one hundred and fifty meters
radius were considered as the spatial units that noticeably increase energy and
economical costs. We considered unsuitable for wetland mitigation all catchment
areas located above the highest point where water flowed frequently. In these areas,
only water pumping could keep water on the wet
raw_name: distance from frequently flowing streams as the water-availability criterion

relationship.weight_scale: 1.5 is the maximum layer weight in the model
relationship.direction: calibration settled the low-cost distance at 450 m and gave distance to frequently flowing streams the maximum weight (1.5) — water availability is the most determinant condition under semi-arid conditions

quote:
Water availability was the most determinant condition for a site to be selected
by the model under semi-arid conditions and the highest weight (1.5) was assigned
to the distance to frequently flowing streams layer. Only the maximum value (1.5)
provided enough enhancement of the parameter in selecting places were water was
available at distances with low implementation cost (established at 450 m).
raw_name: calibrated low-cost distance to frequently flowing streams and its model weight

relationship.direction: slope is RESTRICTIVE for wetland creation: the lower the slope, the less earthwork and the cheaper the project — flat land is favoured on construction-cost grounds

quote:
Slope is a restrictive factor in wetland construction and restoration. The main
design considerations and construction budgets rely on it. The lower the slope,
the cheaper the construction project, as a consequence of the smaller amount
of earthwork needed. Extensive earthwork also involves higher energy expenses.
raw_name: slope as a restrictive construction-cost factor for created wetlands

relationship.direction: in semi-arid agricultural catchments the MOST suitable land for new wetlands is irrigated farmland, where frequent watering favours flooding; low-activity land (abandoned, fallow, rain-fed) is also suitable

quote:
Existing land-use is important in determining the suitability of an area for the
establishment of wetlands. The most suitable areas in this semi-arid territory would
be those affected by irrigation, where frequent watering favours wetland flooding.
Areas with low human activity (abandoned, fallow or rain-fed farmlands) are also
suit
raw_name: existing land use classes suitable for wetland establishment

excluded_classes: developed land (open space, low, medium and high intensity)
relationship.direction: restored/new wetlands may only be placed on the remaining land-cover classes; the listed classes are hard exclusions in the placement model

quote:
No placement of new/
restored wetlands was allowed in any of the simulations in areas with 
the following land cover designations: (1) open water; (2) developed 
land (open space, low intensity, medium intensity, high intensity); (3) 
barren land; (4) shrubland; and (5) wetland.

included_classes: low forest cover or non-forested land (reforestation target)
relationship.direction: planting targets are defined as currently non-forested or low-forest-cover land, identified from forest-loss, impervious-surface and land-cover products

quote:
In this study, adjustments were made to the definitions of target 
areas for afforestation and reforestation based on the regulations set by 
the UNFCCC and Ministry of Forestry (MoFE 2015). Afforested areas 
were defined as non-forested regions of > 50 years. However, owing to 
data limitations, an adjusted approach was adopted in which the target 
areas for afforestation were identified by integrating non-forested 
regional information defined as of 2000. This information was sourced 
from Global Forest Watch data (Hansen et al., 2013), integrated with 
impervious surface data from 1983 to 2000 (Gong et al., 2020), and 
MODIS land-cover data since 2000 (USGS, 2010). Consequently, the 
targeted reforestation areas in this study focused on regions with low 
forest cover or non-forested areas observed from 2000 to 2023.
raw_name: non-forested / low forest cover target areas

relationship.direction: tied ridging performs best on coarser-textured soils in the semi-arid site; on clay (fine-textured) soils ridge tillage can induce waterlogging followed by mass movement and erosion - a negative on heavy clays

quote:
The best CEM techniques were diﬀerent for both sites. In Mbeere
South, tied ridging was the best followed by mulching practice while in
Meru South mulching was the best. The tied ridges in the semi-arid site
were hardly destroyed during the cropping season leading to increased
water content in the soil proﬁle and good crop performance while in the
sub-humid site the ridges were repaired often. On clay soils (in Meru
South), ridge tillage can induce water logging, and later on followed by
mass movement/soil erosion (FAO, 1993). Mulching retained more soil
water content in Meru South since the region received more rainfall
compared with Mbeere South. In addition, soils in Meru South are ﬁne
textured, clay while Mbeere South the soils are coarser. Reduced soil
water retention is observed in coarse textured (Mbeere South) than in
ﬁne-textured soils

A trapezoidal bund consists of a base bund, connected to two side bunds at an angle of about 135° and a distance between the tips of 10 – 100 m. Overflow is discharged around the tips of the side bunds. The wings of the side bunds are pref- erably reinforced with stones. Often they are constructed using machinery. Enclosed areas can reach 1 ha in size (C:A 15:1 – 100:1). The technology is suitable for areas with 200 – 400 mm of annual rainfall.

relationship.direction: reservoirs/tanks are built on gentle slopes

quote: Cultivated reservoirs / tanks are above ground earthen water retention struc- tures. Tanks are constructed on gentile slopes (1 – 10%)

Cultivated reservoirs / tanks are above ground earthen water retention struc- tures. Tanks are constructed on gentile slopes (1 – 10%) by excavating soil and/or building bunds (reservoirs). In this system collected water is either directed from the tank to lower fields or into a below ground tank or shallow well for irrigation (C:A ratio 10:1 – 100:1). When the water of the reservoir is used, the reservoir itself is cropped on soil residual moisture. This system is suitable for areas with 150 – 600 mm annual rainfall.

relationship.direction: small earth/stone storage dams suit semi-arid rainfall

quote: Small earth and stone dams: Rainwater storage systems such as small dams in Ethiopia and Tanzania (known as ndivas), are communally constructed around foot- slopes of hills or along irrigation canals to store the runoff from ephemeral or per- ennial rivers. The reservoirs have neither plastered walls nor covered surfaces. The water is mostly used communally for livestock consumption, and for supplementary irrigation. Ndivas are suitable suitable for areas with 300 – 600 mm of rainfall.

quote: Negarim are small diamond-shaped runoff basins, surrounded by low earth bunds. Runoff infiltrates at the lowest apex, where the trees are planted. Reported sizes of negarim are 100-250 m² in Israel and up to 400 m² in India. As 15-90% of rainfall may be harvested as runoff and used for the tree crop, the catchment to cropping area ratio ranges between 3:1 and 10:1; in flatter catchments and drier areas this may be up to 25:1. They are applied on sloping land (1-20%), however are com- monly found on slopes of 1-5% in areas of 150-500 mm/y of rainfall.

Meskat is rectangular shaped runoff basin. It consists of a catchment area called meskat of about 500 m² in size, and a cropping area called mankaa of about 250 m² (C:A ratio of 2:1). The entire system is surrounded by an approximately 20 cm high bund, and provided with spillways to allow runoff to flow into the mankaa. A meskat can have more than one mankaa arranged in series (see figure below). Surplus runoff spills over one mankaa to the other. Meskats are suitable on slopes of 2-15% and for areas with an annual rainfall of 200 – 400 mm.

relationship.direction: V-shaped bunds are applied up to moderately steep slopes

This technology can be applied on slopes of up to 50%; the steeper the gradient, the more the bunds have to be reinforced by stone (where available).

relationship.outcome_raw: fuel loads and potential wildfire risk

legacy.qualifier: silvopasture reduces grass biomass, litter, and duff depth, thereby reducing fuel loads and wildfire risk; measured at two Washington State ponderosa pine sites

context.note: migrated v1.5.0→v1.6.0 2026-09-30 (deterministic re-shape, method §10); risk_role=livelihood_mitigation; mitigation_potential=moderate; aez temperate_europe removed 2026-10-02 (US study; T7 has no North-American AEZ id)

quote: This study compared forest composition and structure, fuel types, and vegetative biomass between silvopasture and non-grazed managed forests in Washington, U.S. We show that silvopasture management results in reductions in grass biomass, litter, and duff depth when compared to non-grazed managed forest. These findings point to the integrated nature of silvopasture, where management of overstory composition and structure, understory vegetation, and grazing can reduce fuel loads and potential wildfire risk.
raw_name: fuel loads and potential wildfire risk
attribution: Temperate-US scope (Washington State dryland ponderosa pine forest); Mediterranean studies referenced but not the primary site. Findings may not transfer directly to tropical/subtropical or humid-temperate silvopastoral systems.

relationship.outcome_raw: agroforestry offers substantial benefits to women, BUT participation is LOW in enterprises considered men's domain (timber) and HIGH in enterprises with little or no commercial value (indigenous fruit/vegetable collection); participation in soil-fertility management, fodder and woodlots is high by share of female-headed households but LOW by area allocated and number of trees planted

context.note: HEADLINE gender finding: the benefit is real but unevenly captured — a benefit-distribution, not a benefit-magnitude, claim. gender_inequity currently has NO XW route to a T6 target (XW GAP). Narrative review of agroforestry in Africa from a gender perspective (ICRAF); all figures are cited from primary studies, so claim_basis = cited_secondary.

quote: The review shows that agrofor- estry has the potential to offer substantial beneﬁts to women; however, their participation is low in enter- prises that are considered men’s domain, such as timber and high in enterprises that have little or no commercial value, such as collection of indigenous fruits and vegetables. Furthermore, the degree of women’s involvement relative to men in technologies such as soil fertility management, fodder production and woodlots is fairly high in terms of proportion of female-headed households participating but is low as measured by the area they allocate to these activities and the number of trees they plant.

lineage_of: Epaphra 2001; Gerhardt and Nemarundwe 2006; Franzel et al. 2002a; Nyeko et al. 2004
quote: In studies conducted by Epaphra (2001) in Tanzania and Gerhardt and Nemarundwe (2006) in Zimbabwe, it was noted that over 60% of women in Tanzania are responsible for managing tree species planted on farms while over 80% in Zimbabwe are responsible for watering young seedlings. This trend is conﬁrmed by Franzel et al. (2002a) in a study undertaken in Embu, Kenya to determine early stages of adoption of calliandra fodder in the central highlands of Kenya. It was found that although 91% of households using calliandra fodder were male headed, in 89% of these households females were responsible for manag- ing calliandra. A similar scenario was observed in Uganda by Nyeko et al. (2004) whereby in over 80% of households with calliandra, women were involved in management.

quote: Out of seven studies conducted on erosion control, 49 observa- tions were identified for runoff and 49 for soil loss. The studies were conducted in Kenya, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe. Our findings show that agroforestry performed best in terms of erosion reduc- tion ecosystem services, five and ten times better than controls for runoff (RR: 5.0; 95% CI: 3.3-7.9) and soil loss (RR: 9.7; 95% CI: 5.9-17.3). However, these very large effect sizes could also be due to publication bias as demonstrated by the high Kendall’s rank correlation coefficients. If we had found more published studies (larger sample sizes), we expect the effect sizes to be more modest than the figures we reported here. Erosion control with agroforestry was more effective in both humid (RR 7.2; 95% CI 4.8 to 13.9) and semi-arid zones (RR 8.0; 95% CI 4.8 to 16.7) compared to controls. Similarly, erosion control with agroforestry was more effective when either shrubs (RR 6.9; 95% CI 4.6 to 11.4) or trees (RR 11.1; 95% CI 6.1 to 24.7) were planted.

relationship.outcome_raw: agroforestry systems in East Africa stock an average of 24.2 +/- 2.8 Mg C per ha in biomass

context.note: Pooled mean +/- SE (2.8). Systematic review of 185 East-African publications (livelihoods n = 152, carbon n = 43). NOTE: these are carbon STOCKS (Mg C per ha), not sequestration RATES — a rate requires a time denominator the review does not give.

quote: This review shows that agroforestry systems in East Africa stock an average of 24.2 ± 2.8 Mg C ha−1 in biomass and 98.8 ± 12.2 Mg C ha−1 in the soil (Fig. 3). The combined estimate of carbon in biomass and the soil is larger than what was estimated to be the potential carbon storage (29–53 Mg C ha−1) of agrosilvicultural systems in the humid tropics of Africa (Albrecht and Kandji, 2003), but lower than systems with high stem density, large mean tree size, and longer maximum ages i.e. over 60 years reported in Southeast Asia (Roshetko et al., 2007). The difference with earlier estimates is mostly in the soil part where several method­ ological issues need to be considered (Hairiah et al., 2020), such as variation in the soil depth included and changes in soil bulk density that influence which soil is included in a fixed-depth sample (Schrumpf et al., 2011). The amount varies depending on agroforestry practice, ranging from 26.7 ± 7.0 Mg C ha−1 in improved fallows to 153±23 Mg C ha−1 in homegardens.

quote: The overall trend across the studies shows that in the majority of cases (52%) there was a net positive (47%) or neutral (5%) effect of tree presence on food yields or food yield proxies. However, when the results are disaggregated by region, there is a degree of variability (Fig. 5). For example, in the Americas and Asia, tree presence was more likely to enhance food yields with positive effects of trees on yields reported in 58% and 54% of studies for these regions respectively; while in Asia the opposite is the case, with the majority of studies (48%) reporting decreased food yields as a result of tree presence (Fig. 5).

relationship.outcome_raw: in West Africa planting a tree signifies land tenure, so tenants are legally not allowed to plant trees or establish live fences

quote: En África Occidental se generan conflictos de intereses por la implantación de cercas vivas, dado que plantar un árbol tiene significado de tenencia de tierra y alinderación de propiedad. Este conflicto afecta directamente la plantación de cercas vivas ya que, por cuestión legal no se permite a los arrendatarios plantar árboles ni mucho menos establecer cercas vivas, ya que esto podría traer problemas legales al momento de heredar. Por lo tanto, en la mayoría de los casos las cercas vivas no surgirían y tendrían que implementar métodos alternos como el caso de cercas muertas (Levasseur et al., 2004). (English: In West Africa conflicts of interest are generated by the establishment of live fences, since planting a tree has the meaning of land tenure and property demarcation. This conflict directly affects the planting of live fences since, for legal reasons, tenants are not allowed to plant trees, let alone establish live fences, as this could bring legal problems at the time of inheritance. context.region: global review (57 studies, 12 countries, mountain regions)
context.note: Plot-scale meta-analysis by the review authors. quote: Entre los once estudios que midieron la escorrentía en 52 parcelas, todos mostraron una reducción en la escorrentía como resultado de las zanjas de infiltración. El análisis estadístico mostró que las zanjas de infiltración reducen significativamente la escorrentía. En promedio en los estudios anali- zados, las zanjas de infiltración redujeron la escorrentía en un 46.4%. En valores relativos esta reducción representa el 5.7% de la lluvia en promedio. (English: Among the eleven studies that measured runoff on 52 plots, all showed a reduction in runoff as a result of infiltration trenches. The statistical analysis showed that infiltration trenches significantly reduce runoff. On average in the studies analysed, infiltration trenches reduced runoff by 46.4%. In relative values this reduction represents 5.7% of rainfall on average.)

quote: Ocorre que, no entanto, mesmo com as cisternas, o carro-pipa continuou sendo uma realidade neces­ sária no semiárido e as pessoas continuam sujeitas à tentativa de uso político, porque a falta de água as coloca em uma situação muito vulnerável, como no caso das grandes secas plurianuais, explica a coordenadora local do MOC na Bahia: Então, imagina quando seca tudo. E a água da cis­ terna vai acabando. Como é que não dou um pote de água para meus bodes, minhas galinhas? Aí, o vereador chega lá e diz “não se preocupe, eu vou te dar um pipa”. Se, nesse momento, aquele vereador manda uma água para aquela família, ela vai ficar com um sentimento de gratidão [...]. Então, mas a água é um direito, e o direito não pode ser negociado. (Entrevista 5; Arsky 2019). (English: It happens, however, that even with the cisterns, the water truck continued to be a necessary reality in the semi-arid and people remain subject to attempts at political use, because the lack of water puts them in a very vulnerable situation, as in the case of the great multi-year droughts, explains the local MOC coordinator in Bahia: So, imagine when everything dries up. And the cistern water runs out. How can I not give a pot of water to my goats, my chickens? Then the councillor arrives and says 'don't worry, I'll give you a truckload'. If at that moment that councillor sends water to that family, she will feel gratitude [...]. But water is a right, and a right cannot be negotiated. (Interview 5; Arsky 2019).)

relationship.outcome_raw: domestic cistern storage reduces dependence on water trucks and postpones or avoids extreme water-shortage situations (implementer perception + field observation)

Foi muito fácil perceber, na observação direta da pesquisa de campo, como se apresentam as ca­ tegorias dignidade e autonomia. Resultado de um consistente processo de capacitação e conscien­ tização, existe hoje uma verdadeira cultura sobre o gerenciamento da água armazenada na cisterna, e a água de beber armazenada é tratada com zelo e cuidado. Essa reserva adicional, essa poupança, adia ou até mesmo evita as situações limites em que viviam essas famílias. (English: In addition, it conferred autonomy, because the benefiting family 'manages to go without depending on the water truck. It has independence, it has freedom, it doesn't have to sell its vote because of the water truck' (Interview 13; Arsky, 2019), explained the president of ARCAS (BA). It was very easy to perceive, in direct field observation, how the categories of dignity and autonomy present themselves. As a result of a consistent process of training and awareness-raising, there is today a true culture of managing the water stored in the cistern, and the stored drinking water is treated with zeal and care. This additional reserve, this saving, postpones or even avoids the extreme situations in which these families used to live.)

A gente até parou de plantar um pouco, porque estamos poupando para os animais. [...] Se não fosse ela [a água estocada na cisterna] não dava. Porque a água da EMBASA [Empresa Baiana de Águas e Saneamento] não dá, porque passa da taxa. E, também, nós nem teríamos como armazenar, porque a água vem de oito em oito dias, e nós aqui em cima somos o último a receber, então quando chega nossa vez, já é hora de acabar de novo [...]. A água que tá na cisterna é da chuva e ainda tem como segurar alguns meses. (English: We had difficulty with water, because from where we live to the fields, to the tanks, it is quite far, and now not, because we got the cistern with a pump, and the extension comes with the project itself. [...] It was good after this water. Even right now, the clay tanks are dry and the animals are drinking from the cistern. We even stopped planting a bit, because we are saving it for the animals. [...] If it weren't for it [the water stored in the cistern] it wouldn't be possible. Because the EMBASA [Bahia water and sanitation company] water isn't enough, because it exceeds the fee. quote: De todo modo, das mais de 1 milhão de cisternas de consumo e produção construídas, a maio­ ria encontra-se no meio rural (tabela 4) e, nesse sentido, é inegável sua significativa contribuição para a ampliação do acesso à água na região. Considerando-se que em 2017 aproximadamente 446 mil estabelecimentos agropecuários no semiárido não possuíam acesso à nenhuma fonte hídrica,16 havendo um número de mais de 1 milhão de cisternas construídas, boa parte das quais no semiárido e no meio rural, é fácil concluir que o número de estabelecimentos, principalmente familiares (tabela 4), e, consequentemente, pessoas sem acesso à água seria muito maior. Esses dados confirmam que, justamente onde esperado, no meio rural, as cisternas contribuem de modo evidente, com a consecução da meta 6.1 do ODS da água. (English: In any case, of the more than 1 million consumption and production cisterns built, most are in rural areas (table 4) and, in this sense, their significant contribution to expanding access to water in the region is undeniable. Considering that in 2017 approximately 446 thousand agricultural establishments in the semi-arid had no access to any water source,16 with more than 1 million cisterns built, a good part of them in the semi-arid and in rural areas, it is easy to conclude that the number of establishments, mainly family farms (table 4), and consequently of people without access to water would be much greater. These data confirm that, exactly where expected, in rural areas, cisterns contribute clearly to achieving SDG target 6.1 on water.)

context.note: hazard = in-season dry spells (veranicos), i.e. agricultural drought; institutional statement, no data in passage; barreiro = small earth reservoir fed by a micro-catchment; COI: Embrapa Semiarido self-assessment of technologies it developed/promotes

quote: tre estas tecnologias, o uso da irrigação de salvação tem reduzido os riscos da exploração agrícola em anos cuja precipitação pluviométrica é irregular, proporcionando até duas colheitas em anos considerados normais de chuvas. Segundo Porto et al. (1983), no Semi-Árido brasi- leiro, três em cada dez anos são considerados normais com relação à quantidade e à distribuição das chuvas. Define-se a irrigação de salvação como a lâmina de água aplicada à cul- tura nos veranicos que comumente ocorrem durante o período chuvoso na região Nordeste, de forma a não permitir que a cultura sofra estresse hídrico e, em alguns casos, morra. No Semi-Árido brasileiro, após as pri- meiras chuvas, é comum ocorrerem períodos de 20 a 30 dias sem novas chuvas, comprometendo seriamente a germinação e outras fases de de- senvolvimento das culturas. (English: [Am]ong these technologies, supplemental (salvation) irrigation has reduced the risks of farming in years with irregular rainfall, allowing up to two harvests in years considered normal. According to Porto et al. (1983), in the Brazilian semi-arid three in every ten years are considered normal in rainfall quantity and distribution. Salvation irrigation is defined as the depth of water applied to the crop during the dry spells (veranicos) that commonly occur during the rainy season in the Northeast, so as not to let the crop suffer water stress and, in some cases, die. In the Brazilian semi-arid, after the first rains, periods of 20 to 30 days without new rain are common, seriously compromising germination and other crop development phases.)

context.note: Bundle includes rangeland closure + gully stone-filling, not bunds alone.

quote: Bergaoui et Albergel en Tunisie semi-aride (2000) ont étudié sur un bassin montagneux de 780 ha l’effet d’un aménagement complexe comportant la mise en défens des parcours, des cordons de pierres isohypses formant terrasses progressives (60% de la surface) et l’empierrement des ravines. En comparant 71 crues à une pointe, avant et après l’aménagement, ils ont montré le rallongement du temps de montée, l’étalement des crues (temps de base doublé), l’écrêtement des débits de pointe (=1/3), donc des transports solides et la réduction de 50% du volume ruisselé. (English: Bergaoui and Albergel in semi-arid Tunisia (2000) studied, on a 780 ha mountain catchment, the effect of a complex treatment comprising rangeland closure, contour stone bunds forming progressive terraces (60% of the area) and stone-filling of gullies. Comparing 71 single-peak floods before and after treatment, they showed lengthening of the rise time, spreading of floods (base time doubled), clipping of peak discharges (=1/3), hence of sediment transport, and a 50% reduction of runoff volume.)

quote: C'est ainsi qu'en 1973 DELWAULLE signale à Allokoto, dans la même région, que la banquette isohypse, par rapport au témoin (culture traditionnelle) permet de multi- plier la production par 2,3 tout en divisant le ruissellement par 37 et l'érosion par 150 (moyenne sur 2 ans et un couple de parcelle de 0,4 ha). (English: Thus in 1973 DELWAULLE reports at Allokoto, in the same region, that the contour banquette, compared with the control (traditional cropping), makes it possible to multiply production by 2.3 while dividing runoff by 37 and erosion by 150 (mean over 2 years and one pair of 0.4 ha plots).)
